narration_lines: Each millimetre of rain means one litre of water on a square metre.
Accumulated rainfall is rain added up over a set time, like one whole day.
Radar maps show where rain was falling a short time ago. The key explains the colours.
The water level tells how high the river surface is on its gauge. Rising or falling matters most.
A low-lying area is low, flat ground. Water collects there first.
A closed road keeps cars away from deep water. This is a road closure. Barriers are helpers.
A flash flood arrives quickly, in hills or in towns. Families move to the marked safe high ground and wait.
Good listeners ask three questions. How much rain? Where is the water going? Is the level rising?
Now the news makes sense. Next time we hear it, we can explain it.
